reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, batch 1

samples_reviewed.question_text: Look at the November 2025 date chart. What day of the week is November 4?
Look at the January 2025 date chart. What day of the week is January 10?
Look at the July 2025 date chart. What day of the week is July 17?
Look at the May 2025 date chart. What day of the week is May 14?
Look at the February 2025 date chart. What day of the week is February 13?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: This node's samples are a direct match: 'Look at the January 2025 date chart. What day of the week is January 10?' requires the student to read a real calendar to determine a day, exactly as the competency states.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: calendar registers 2 axes/8 combos per variant_registry, exhaustively checked by validate_matrix separately; the 5 illustrative seeds here span 5 different months (November, January, July, May, February), showing reasonable breadth.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Sentences stay at or under 13 words ('Look at the February 2025 date chart. What day of the week is February 13?'), within the 15-word grade-1 cap, and the task is a single calendar-lookup step appropriate for grade 1 quarter 4.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: 8 registered combos across 2 axes, evidenced here by 5 different months and dates queried, plausibly supports the calendar-navigation mastery this node targets.

competency_alignment.rationale: The task stays confined to locating a specific day from a given date on a calendar, without drifting into date arithmetic, e.g. days-until, that would belong to a later competency.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Using specific real 2025 calendar months/dates is an appropriate, concrete real-world scale for a grade-1 calendar-reading competency.
